# A method that takes `response` owns the response, so muxt writes no status
# code and no redirect for that route. A template calling .Redirect*, or
# .StatusCode, on such a route is asking for something that cannot happen: the
# field is set on TemplateData and never read.
#
# It used to generate quietly. The template parsed, generate and check both
# exited 0, and the redirect simply did not occur at runtime.
#
# .StatusCode has the same problem for the same reason, so it is reported the
# same way.

! muxt generate --use-receiver-type=T
cmpenv stderr want-err.txt

# check reports it too, so it fails in CI before anyone runs the route. Its
# second complaint is that nothing generated the handlers, which follows from
# the first: generate stopped.
! muxt check
cmpenv stderr want-check.txt

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- template.gohtml --
{{- define "GET /with-response WithResponse(ctx, response)" -}}
	{{- .RedirectSeeOther "/elsewhere" -}}
{{- end -}}

{{- define "GET /status WithStatus(ctx, response)" -}}
	{{- .StatusCode 404 -}}
{{- end -}}

{{- define "GET /without-response WithoutResponse(ctx)" -}}
	{{- .RedirectSeeOther "/elsewhere" -}}
{{- end -}}
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"context"
	"embed"
	"html/template"
	"net/http"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templatesFS embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templatesFS, "*"))

type T struct{}

func (T) WithResponse(ctx context.Context, response http.ResponseWriter) any { return nil }
func (T) WithStatus(ctx context.Context, response http.ResponseWriter) any   { return nil }
func (T) WithoutResponse(ctx context.Context) any                           { return nil }
